adaptationNotes: Earliest documented 2009 prototype with only cobblestone and grass placement. No mod loader, JSON recipes, entities, or resource packs existed. Only conceptual documentation or direct decompiled class notes are possible.
Added dirt, planks, saplings, and block selection. No mod loader or external asset pipeline exists.
First public Classic release. No mod loader APIs, JSON models, or entity registries exist; custom blocks require replacing core terrain.png tiles and patching obfuscated applet classes.
Classic creative era. No Forge, Fabric, or JSON systems exist.
Introduced health and classic mobs (Zombies, Skeletons, Creepers). No external mod loader or data-driven definitions exist.
Final Classic release. Modern mod loaders and JSON data packs are unsupported.
Introduced crafting, tools, and finite worlds. Modding required raw bytecode edits before Risugami's ModLoader existed.
Introduced infinite procedural worlds and chunk saving. Still predates formal mod loaders.
Alpha versions use numeric block IDs (0–255), terrain.png sprite sheets, and direct Block/Item subclassing without JSON models or modern Forge registries.
Supports BaseMod / ModLoader hooks with numeric IDs and sprite indices in terrain.png / gui/items.png. No JSON recipes, loot tables, or resource packs.
Uses Risugami's ModLoader (BaseMod) with ModLoader.RegisterBlock and ModLoader.AddRecipe. No Forge API or JSON data packs.
Classic golden-age modding target using ModLoader + early Minecraft Forge 1.0.x sprite-sheet APIs. Uses numeric block/item IDs and Java-coded recipes; no JSON models or loot tables.
Uses ModLoader / early Forge 1.1.x. Client-server split did not exist in singleplayer yet.
First official Java 1.0 release. Uses ModLoader / early Forge sprite-sheet APIs and numeric IDs; no Gradle/ForgeGradle workspace or JSON assets.
Pre-integrated-server Forge (client & server mods separated). Uses BaseMod / NetworkMod and 256x256 sprite sheets.
Uses @Mod, @Init, GameRegistry.registerBlock, mcmod.info, and sprite sheets. Predates ForgeGradle and individual texture PNGs (1.5+).
Introduced individual PNG textures per block/item via IconRegister, still uses numeric IDs and Java-coded recipes.
Introduced Resource Packs (assets/<modid>/textures/...) and first ForgeGradle support; still uses numeric IDs via Configuration.

updateName: The Update that Changed the World
adaptationNotes: Iconic Forge modding milestone. Removed manual numeric IDs in favor of GameRegistry.registerBlock/registerItem with string names. Recipes & models are Java-coded (JSON block models arrived in 1.8; JSON recipes in 1.12).
Introduced JSON blockstates and item/block models; recipes remain Java-coded via GameRegistry.addRecipe.
Uses IForgeRegistry / GameRegistry.register(IForgeRegistryEntry) and JSON loot tables (introduced in 1.9).
Major Forge LTS version. Uses RegistryEvent.Register<T>, ResourceLocation, JSON recipes, JSON loot tables, and mcmod.info. Note: Fabric and NeoForge do not support 1.12.2.
Forge switched to META-INF/mods.toml and DeferredRegister; Fabric launched with fabric.mod.json and Yarn mappings.
Introduced data-driven custom dimensions (dimension & dimension_type JSON), Official Mojang Mappings on Forge, and DeferredRegister.
Requires Java 17. Uses Registries / DeferredRegister on Forge and Registry.register on Fabric.
Uses CreativeModeTabEvent / ItemGroupEvents for creative tabs and BuiltInRegistries on Fabric.
Major modding LTS target. Supports Forge 47.x, early NeoForge 47.x, and Fabric with BuiltInRegistries / DeferredRegister.
NeoForge uses META-INF/mods.toml (migrated to neoforge.mods.toml in 1.20.5+) and DeferredRegister.createBlocks / createItems.
Upgraded runtime to Java 21, replaced ItemStack NBT with DataComponents, and switched NeoForge to META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml.
Requires Java 21. Uses ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(modId, name), DataComponents, and data-driven enchantments/jukebox songs.
Primary 1.21.x modding baseline for NeoForge 21.1 and Fabric.
Includes Bundles and 1.21.2/1.21.3 BlockBehaviour.Properties setId requirement on item/block keys.
Introduced assets/<modid>/items/<item>.json client item definition files alongside models/item/*.json.
Added biome-specific farm mob variants, firefly bushes, and updated equipment/spawn data formats.
Follow-up patch to 1.21.6–1.21.7 Chase the Skies drop (happy ghasts, craftable saddles, locator bar).
Copper Age game drop (Copper Golem, copper gear/tools/armor, copper chests, shelves).
Final 1.21.x game drop before Mojang's 2026 year-based version shift. Added spears, rideable nautiluses, and netherite horse armor.
First Java Edition release under Mojang's 2026 year-based version numbering (Tiny Takeover: overhauled baby mobs, golden dandelion, craftable name tags).
Added Sulfur Caves biome, sulfur cubes, sulfur/cinnabar block sets, and experimental Vulkan renderer support.
Major 2026 game drop featuring Dappled Forest biome, poplar wood sets, explorer camps, straw beds, and cushions.
Latest stable Java Edition live release branch as of November 2026. Fully compatible with 26.3 NeoForge and Fabric APIs.
26.4 remains in active Snapshot testing as of late November 2026; mod loader APIs may shift before final stable 26.4 release.
Original Pocket Edition release. Behavior Packs, Resource Packs, manifest.json, and Script API did not exist until PE 0.16.0 (2016).
Official Mojang JSON Add-ons (.mcpack / .mcaddon) are not supported in PE 0.8.1. Target PE 0.16.0+ or Bedrock 1.16.100+ for official add-ons.
Predates the official Add-on system introduced in PE 0.16.0. No Behavior Packs or Script API support.

requiredRuntime: Bedrock Add-on Format v1 (No Custom Items/Blocks/Script API)
adaptationNotes: Introduced Behavior & Resource Packs for modifying vanilla entity behaviors and textures. Custom blocks, custom items, custom recipes, and Script API are NOT supported in 0.16.0.
Unified Pocket/Windows 10/Console as Bedrock Edition. Supports vanilla entity modification and resource packs; custom blocks/items and Script API are unsupported.
Added custom entity definitions and Geometry 1.10/1.12; custom items/blocks remain experimental and Script API is unavailable.
Major milestone enabling data-driven custom blocks and items in Behavior Packs. Uses older Molang/item formats; @minecraft/server Script API is not yet supported.
Uses mojang-minecraft experimental namespace if scripting is enabled; prefer standard JSON components for stability.
Stable @minecraft/server 1.1.0 scripting introduced; custom item/block format_version 1.19.80.
Supports custom components v2, attachable armor/weapons, and @minecraft/server 1.10.0.
Supports stable block & item customComponents in Script API without experimental toggles.
The Garden Awakens parity update with Pale Garden / Creaking and @minecraft/server 1.16.0.
Spring to Life game drop with expanded mob variants and Script API 1.18.0.
Introduced Vibrant Visuals deferred lighting/PBR texture sets and @minecraft/server 2.0.0.
The Copper Age drop with Copper Golem, copper tools/armor, and Script API 2.2.0.
Final 1.21.x Bedrock release before the 2026 year-based version shift.
First Bedrock release under 2026 year-based numbering; manifest min_engine_version [26, 10, 0].
Sulfur Caves biome, sulfur cubes, and Bedrock 26.30 schema compatibility.
Dappled Forest biome, poplar wood sets, and cushions; manifest min_engine_version [26, 50, 0].
Added experimental Ice Caves biome, Frostbite mob, and 600+ bug fixes; min_engine_version [26, 60, 0].
Latest official Bedrock Edition release through November 2026. Full support for Behavior Packs, Resource Packs, custom components, and Script API.
